_metadata.description: Per-workflow saving assumptions used by the parametric cost models. These are the agent's working assumptions — initial values are derived from evercam_role, evidence data, and usage data. They are explicitly provisional and intended to be refined through training conversations with Evercam domain experts.
_metadata.status: provisional — no assumptions have been validated through training mode
_metadata.update_frequency: Refined through training mode conversations. Each update should record who validated, when, and the rationale for the change.

assumption_status_values.provisional: Initial estimate, not yet discussed with domain experts
assumption_status_values.discussed: Has been reviewed in training mode but not formally signed off
assumption_status_values.validated: Formally accepted by a named Evercam domain expert
assumption_status_values.contested: Experts disagree on this value — range widened, needs further data

site_visit_avoidance.description: Evercam replaces or reduces physical site visits with remote viewing. The baseline cost is the number of visits × cost per visit. The saving is the proportion of visits that Evercam eliminates.

automated_content.description: Evercam eliminates manual effort for recurring content production (progress photos, time-lapse, marketing videos). The baseline cost is the manual time per deliverable × frequency.
automated_content.formula: saving = manual_hours_per_deliverable × deliverables_per_month × project_duration_months × hourly_rate × evercam_reduction_pct

security_theft.description: Evercam prevents security incidents or reduces their cost through deterrence, faster investigation, and evidence for insurance/police. The baseline is incident frequency × cost per incident.

safety_incident.description: Evercam speeds safety incident investigation, supports proactive monitoring, and provides evidence for claim defence. Saving comes from faster investigations and reduced/defended claims.

dispute_claims.description: Evercam provides visual evidence that resolves or prevents disputes with subcontractors, suppliers, and clients. Saving from faster resolution, avoided escalation, and prevented overcharges.

rework_prevention.description: Evercam enables early detection of deviations from design, reducing rework costs. Saving is a fraction of the rework that would otherwise occur.

risk_reduction.description: Low-probability, high-consequence events whose expected cost is reduced by Evercam's monitoring, deterrence, or evidence capability. Calculated as expected value (probability × cost). Presented separately from operational savings in the output document under 'Risk Mitigation Value'.
risk_reduction.formula: annual_risk_without = event_probability × event_cost; annual_risk_with = (event_probability × (1 - probability_reduction_pct)) × (event_cost × (1 - cost_mitigation_pct)); saving = (annual_risk_without - annual_risk_with) × (project_duration_months / 12)
risk_reduction.presentation_note: These line items appear in a separate 'Risk Mitigation Value' section, not in the operational savings total. Payback period is calculated from operational savings only. ROI ratio uses combined value.

narrative_framings.hs_director: Annualised risk reduction — how they naturally think about safety investment
narrative_framings.qs_commercial: Expected value of downside protection — insurance pricing framing
narrative_framings.leadership: Maximum exposure reduced from £X to £Y — cap-and-floor framing
narrative_framings.default: If this event occurs, Evercam reduces the cost from £X to £Y. Across the project duration, the expected value of this protection is £Z.

visit_duration_fraction.rationale: Typical PM site visit is half a day including travel. Customer interview confirmed 7–15 min capture time but total visit including travel, meetings, and follow-up is ~4 hours.

evercam_reduction_pct.rationale: Replacement role — Evercam is the primary tool for this workflow. Conservative: PM still visits 70% of the time but visits are shorter. Base: half of visits replaced by remote check. Optimistic: only critical visits remain physical. Supported by 6,319 active LiveView users across 611 companies (PostHog 90-day data).
evercam_reduction_pct.calibration_note: This is the single highest-impact assumption in most ROI calculations. Prioritise for training mode validation.

visit_duration_fraction.rationale: Schedule verification visits are typically shorter — focused on specific areas, not whole-site walks. ~2 hours.

evercam_reduction_pct.rationale: Supporting role — Evercam assists but doesn't replace physical verification. PM still needs to walk critical path areas. But timeline/footage review can replace many routine check-ins. 995 Timeline users across 271 companies (PostHog).

occurrences_per_week.rationale: Typically weekly programme review meetings drive this verification.

visit_duration_fraction.rationale: Owner/stakeholder visits are typically half-day events including travel, tour, and debrief.

evercam_reduction_pct.rationale: Replacement role — Evercam is the primary reporting tool. Time-lapse and shared camera access can replace most routine progress visits. Owner still visits for key milestones. 70 evidence count (highest). Median 14 camera shares per project confirms broad stakeholder access.

stakeholder_visits_per_month.rationale: Typically fortnightly or monthly owner/investor visits, plus ad-hoc requests.

assumptions.additional_saving_note: Also saves PM time preparing for visits (assembling reports, doing pre-visit walk). Estimated 2–4 hours prep per stakeholder visit.

visit_duration_fraction.rationale: Interior walk-throughs require physical presence — but with 360 captures, remote stakeholders don't need to be there.

evercam_reduction_pct.rationale: Replacement role for remote review, but someone still does the physical capture (or robot will). Value is in avoiding *other people's* visits to review interiors. 1,335 active 360 users across 229 companies (PostHog).

workflow_assumptions.workflow_name: Automated Daily / Weekly Progress Photo Distribution

manual_hours_per_deliverable.rationale: Without automation: capture photo, select/edit, compose email, send to distribution list. ~30 mins per cycle. Customer interview confirmed 25 photos per day as SOP.

deliverables_per_month.rationale: Daily distribution on working days. Some projects do weekly (4/month).

evercam_reduction_pct.rationale: Replacement role — fully automated via Snapmail. 551 active snapmails sending ~7,500 emails/month. Average 3.1 recipients. Near-total elimination of manual effort.

assumptions.staff_role_note: The person who would otherwise take/send photos is typically the site manager or superintendent, not the PM.

manual_hours_per_deliverable.rationale: Without Evercam: hire a videographer or manually compile footage, edit, produce. A professional time-lapse production is typically a full day's work per deliverable.

deliverables_per_project.rationale: Typical: one per quarter or per major milestone. 19,678 timelapses across ~3,030 projects ≈ 6.5 per project average.

evercam_reduction_pct.rationale: Replacement role — Evercam generates time-lapses automatically from camera footage. Some manual curation/branding still needed. 2,278 active timelapse users (PostHog).

assumptions.alternative_cost_note: For some customers the alternative isn't manual production — it's not producing time-lapses at all. In that case the ROI framing shifts from cost saving to value creation (content they couldn't otherwise afford).

manual_hours_per_deliverable.rationale: Without Evercam: arrange site visit for photographer/videographer, shoot, edit, post. Or marketing team creates content from scratch.

deliverables_per_month.rationale: Typical social media posting cadence for construction companies. Some do more, many do less.

evercam_reduction_pct.rationale: Replacement role — time-lapse and camera footage provides ready-made content. Still needs branding/captioning.

assumptions.staff_role_note: Cost basis varies — marketing staff rate if dedicated marketing team, PM rate if PM handles this.

workflow_assumptions.workflow_name: Drone-Based Site Survey & Aerial Progress Capture

manual_hours_per_deliverable.rationale: Without Evercam: hire drone operator, fly, process imagery, upload to separate platform. Or use a third-party survey service.

deliverables_per_month.rationale: Fortnightly to monthly aerial surveys typical.

evercam_reduction_pct.rationale: Supporting/replacement — Evercam consolidates drone data onto the same platform as all other visual data. Eliminates separate processing pipeline. Drone still needs to be flown. 1,450 active drone users across 264 companies (PostHog).

assumptions.alternative_cost_note: Some customers compare against third-party drone survey services which charge per-flight. In that case the cost model is: Evercam cost vs. third-party cost, not time saving.

incidents_per_year.rationale: CIOB: 92% of sites experience theft. Average loss £10K–£50K/year per site. Number of discrete incidents varies widely. Conservative assumes a well-secured site.

avg_incident_cost.note: Use the per-incident value, not the annual aggregate. Divide annual loss by incidents_per_year to get per-incident.

incidents_prevented_pct.rationale: Replacement role — Evercam is the primary investigation tool. Deterrence effect of visible cameras. Recovery enabled by footage evidence. But cameras don't physically prevent theft.

investigation_time_saved_hours.rationale: Without footage: half a day to two days of investigation, witness interviews, police coordination. With footage: review in 1–2 hours, export clip. Saving ~6–8 hours per incident.

incidents_per_year.rationale: Includes attempted intrusions, after-hours access by unauthorised persons, and suspicious activity. Higher frequency than theft because includes non-theft security events.

incidents_prevented_pct.rationale: Supporting role — Evercam provides evidence after the fact and supports monitoring, but is typically not the primary security system. Motion detection feature used on 24 completed projects.

investigation_time_saved_hours.rationale: Footage narrows the investigation window. Without it: review all access points, interview night watch, check for damage. With it: review footage, identify timeline.

assumptions.guard_cost_offset_note: Some customers use Evercam as a partial substitute for night security guards. If applicable, this is an additional saving line: guard_hours_saved × guard_hourly_rate. Not modelled by default as it depends on the customer's security setup.

workflow_assumptions.workflow_name: Gate Access Control & Vehicle Movement Monitoring

manual_hours_saved_per_week.rationale: Without ANPR gate report: manual logging of vehicle entries, physical docket checking, manual reconciliation of deliveries. Gate report automates this. 5.1M plate reads across 60 cameras in the Evercam AI DB. 1,365 active GateReport users (PostHog).

evercam_reduction_pct.rationale: Replacement role — ANPR completely automates vehicle logging. Manual effort reduced to reviewing reports and handling exceptions. 85 completed projects used gate_report feature.

assumptions.delivery_dispute_prevention_note: Gate report data also prevents delivery disputes (cross-reference with Template E workflows #42). Avoid double-counting this benefit.
assumptions.model_override: This workflow uses a hybrid model: part automated_content (time saved on manual logging) and part security_theft (unauthorised access prevention). The formula is: (manual_hours_per_week × weeks × site_manager_rate × reduction_pct) + (unauthorised_access_incidents_prevented × incident_cost).

incidents_per_year.rationale: Reportable + non-reportable incidents requiring formal investigation. HSE: construction non-fatal injury rate 2.5%. On a project with 50 workers: ~1.25 injuries/year. But investigations also triggered by near-misses and property damage.

investigation_hours_without_evercam.rationale: A formal incident investigation without footage: scene examination, witness interviews (often conflicting), reconstruction, report writing. Typically 2 full days of H&S manager time.

investigation_hours_with_evercam.rationale: With footage: review recording, identify sequence of events, export evidence, write report. Reconstruction is visual rather than testimonial.

investigation_time_saved_pct.rationale: Derived: (16-6)/16 = 62.5%. Footage-based investigation is dramatically faster because it eliminates the need to reconcile conflicting witness accounts.

assumptions.claim_defence_note: Overlap with #40 (Workers' Comp Defence). The investigation saving is counted here; the claim value defence is counted under #40. No double-counting.

safety_walks_replaced_per_week.rationale: Physical safety walks that can be partially replaced by remote camera review. Not all walks can be replaced — hands-on inspection still required for many checks.

walk_duration_hours.rationale: Typical safety walk: 1–2 hours depending on site size.

evercam_reduction_pct.rationale: Supporting role — cameras can spot PPE non-compliance and unsafe behaviour from fixed positions, but cannot replace physical safety walks entirely. PPE monitoring feature only on 5 completed projects (very early). Only 62 SmartSearch users (PostHog), though that capability is growing.
evercam_reduction_pct.calibration_note: This saving percentage may increase significantly as AI-powered safety detection matures. Current estimate is conservative.

workflow_assumptions.workflow_name: Workers' Compensation & False Injury Claim Defence

claimable_incidents_per_year.rationale: Not all incidents result in claims. Estimate: 1 claim per year on a mid-size project. HSE: average employer cost per injury £21,907.

claims_defended_or_reduced_pct.rationale: Supporting role — footage doesn't prevent claims but significantly strengthens defence. Can prove contributory negligence, dispute false claims, or demonstrate that safety protocols were followed. Major value in reducing settlement amounts rather than eliminating claims entirely.

disputes_per_year.rationale: Labour attendance disputes scale with subcontractor count. On a project with 20 subcontractors, at least a few will have contested daywork or attendance claims per year.

disputes_per_subcontractor_per_year.rationale: Alternative scaling: 20% of subcontractors will have at least one attendance dispute per year.

avg_dispute_value.currency_note: In project's local currency. These are per-dispute values — the cost of investigation + the overcharge if undetected. Customer interview: $500–$7,000 per instance.

disputes_resolved_by_footage_pct.rationale: Supporting role — footage provides timestamp evidence of who was on site and when. Directly applicable to attendance disputes. Does not resolve all disputes (some are about quality, not presence).

disputes_per_year.rationale: Invoice disputes are more frequent than attendance disputes. Every subcontractor submits monthly applications; discrepancies are common.

avg_resolution_cost_without_footage.currency_note: In project's local currency. Includes QS investigation time + management time + potential adjudication referral cost.

evercam_reduction_pct.rationale: Supporting role — footage and gate report data provide evidence to resolve disputes faster and avoid escalation. KCL data: 75% of claimed sum recovered in adjudication. Early resolution avoids the £4,500 referral cost.

workflow_assumptions.workflow_name: Delay, EOT & Weather Event Documentation for Claims

delay_events_per_project.rationale: Weather events and other delay causes requiring formal documentation. Varies hugely by project type and climate.

ld_exposure_per_delay_day.note: 0.5% of contract value per week, divided by 7 for daily rate. From project_ratios.json.

days_recovered_per_event.rationale: Footage proves weather conditions, demonstrates contractor good faith, supports EOT claim. Customer interview: 'I was able to show the owner an eight-week drop in production' — footage was used to recover schedule time by proving the delay was owner-caused.

assumptions.roi_description_note: The existing roi_description says: 'Measure days recovered by proving weather delays. Multiply by liquidated damages per day to calculate ROI.' This is the most directly quantifiable ROI model — LD savings can be enormous.

variation_claims_per_project.rationale: Variations are frequent on most projects. Each one can be disputed. Scales with project complexity and subcontractor count.

claims_resolved_by_footage_pct.rationale: Supporting role — footage shows what work was done and when, which can validate or refute variation claims. Not all variations are visual (some are specification-based).

delivery_discrepancies_per_month.rationale: Discrepancies between delivery dockets and actual quantities received. Customer interview confirmed this as a frequent issue: 'Material arrives on site, and we don't know what's on site.'

avg_overcharge_value.currency_note: In project's local currency. Per-discrepancy value.

evercam_reduction_pct.rationale: Supporting role — Gate Report with ANPR provides timestamped vehicle entry/exit logs. Cross-reference with delivery dockets. 5.1M ANPR records, 85 completed projects with gate_report.

workflow_assumptions.workflow_name: BIM vs. Reality Comparison & Design Verification

rework_rate_pct.note: Uses conservative/base/optimistic from the benchmark data (4%/6%/10%).

early_detection_pct.rationale: Percentage of rework that could be detected earlier through BIM-to-reality comparison. Conservative: catches 5% of rework before it's too late. Optimistic: catches 20%. Note: BIM comparison is one of many rework prevention tools; Evercam's specific contribution is catching visual deviations from the model.

evercam_contribution_pct.rationale: When Evercam's BIM overlay detects a deviation, Evercam gets full credit for that detection. The early_detection_pct already scopes the fraction of detectable deviations. 95 completed projects with 4d_bim feature; 1,208 active BIM users across 253 companies (PostHog).

assumptions.note: On a £20M project with 6% rework rate and 10% early detection: saving = £20M × 0.06 × 0.10 = £120,000. This can be a very large line item even with conservative assumptions.

visit_duration_fraction.rationale: Portfolio managers visiting satellite sites typically spend most of a day per visit including inter-site travel. Longer than single-site visits because of travel between dispersed locations.

evercam_reduction_pct.rationale: Replacement role — Evercam is the primary tool enabling remote oversight across multiple sites. Portfolio managers can check all sites from a single dashboard rather than driving between them. Very strong model: saving is multiplied by number_of_sites. Physical visits still needed for critical milestones and issues.

visits_per_site_per_month.rationale: Portfolio/regional managers typically visit each site fortnightly. Some sites get weekly visits, remote sites monthly.

assumptions.travel_cost_note: Inter-site travel costs are typically higher than single-site commute costs. For geographically dispersed portfolios, may include flights/hotels.
assumptions.formula_note: Total saving = per-site saving × number_of_sites. The number_of_sites parameter comes from the customer profile.

manual_hours_per_deliverable.rationale: Compiling a handover pack without Evercam: gather photos from multiple sources, organise by date/area, compile progress evidence, create as-built visual records. Typically 2 full days of PM/admin time per handover pack.

deliverables_per_project.rationale: One major handover pack per project at close-out. Some phased projects may have 2–3 sectional handovers.

evercam_reduction_pct.rationale: Supporting role — Evercam provides a complete, timestamped visual record that dramatically reduces the effort of assembling handover documentation. Still requires curation, formatting, and non-visual documentation.

assumptions.additional_value_note: Beyond time saving, Evercam improves handover quality — providing continuous visual evidence rather than sporadic manual photos. This can reduce post-handover disputes.

manual_hours_per_deliverable.rationale: Without Evercam: visit site, take before photo, return later for after photo, match angles, compile comparison. With Compare tool: select two timestamps, generate side-by-side. ~45 mins manual effort saved per comparison.

deliverables_per_month.rationale: Typical usage: 1–2 comparisons per week for progress reports, stakeholder updates, and milestone documentation. 7,522 compares across 1,318 projects = ~5.7 per project total, but active users generate them more frequently.

evercam_reduction_pct.rationale: Replacement role — Compare tool completely replaces the manual process of taking matched before/after photos. Near-total automation. 7,522 compares across 1,318 projects confirms widespread adoption.

manual_hours_per_deliverable.rationale: A snag inspection without 360 captures: walk area, photograph each defect, note location, compile list with annotated photos. With Evercam 360: capture area once, review and annotate remotely. Saving ~2 hours per inspection round.

deliverables_per_month.rationale: During fit-out/finishing phase, snag inspections happen weekly or more frequently. This workflow is concentrated in the final 3–6 months of the project.

evercam_reduction_pct.rationale: Supporting role — 360 captures reduce the number of physical revisits needed to document snags, but physical inspection is still required for many defects (touch, function tests). Most value in reducing revisits for visual snags.

assumptions.phase_note: This workflow is active primarily during the final 20–30% of the project timeline. Model should weight duration accordingly.

workflow_assumptions.workflow_name: RFI & Issue Logging with Visual Evidence

manual_hours_per_deliverable.rationale: Creating an RFI with visual evidence without Evercam: visit area, photograph issue, return to office, attach to RFI form, describe location. With Evercam: screenshot from camera, annotate, attach. Saving ~30 mins per RFI.

deliverables_per_month.rationale: Typical mid-size project generates 5–15 RFIs per month that benefit from visual evidence. Not all RFIs need photos, but most design/coordination issues do.

evercam_reduction_pct.rationale: Supporting role — Evercam provides readily available screenshots and clips that can be attached to RFIs without a site visit. Particularly valuable when the person raising the RFI is not on site (designer, PM, client).

assumptions.additional_value_note: Beyond time saving, visual RFIs are resolved faster because the reviewer can see the issue immediately. This reduces RFI turnaround time, which has schedule implications not captured in this model.

manual_hours_per_deliverable.rationale: Without Evercam: PM walks site before OAC meeting to verify progress, takes photos, assembles slide deck or report with visual updates. Customer interview confirmed PMs spending significant time on meeting prep. With Evercam: pull screenshots/clips from cameras, generate comparisons. ~2 hours saved per meeting cycle.

deliverables_per_month.rationale: Weekly OAC/progress meetings are standard on most construction projects. Some projects have fortnightly meetings.

evercam_reduction_pct.rationale: Supporting role — Evercam provides visual content for meetings but PM still needs to analyse progress, prepare narrative, and lead the meeting. The saving is in content gathering, not meeting facilitation.

assumptions.staff_role_note: This is PM time — typically the most expensive person on the project team aside from the project director.

manual_hours_per_deliverable.rationale: This is a replacement model where the alternative is hiring a videographer, not spending internal time. Use alternative_cost instead.

alternative_cost_per_deliverable.rationale: Professional videographer for construction completion video: 1 day shooting + 1–2 days editing. Rates vary from £1,500 (basic) to £8,000+ (high-end corporate production). Conservative estimate reflects a basic production.

deliverables_per_project.rationale: One completion/handover video per project. The time-lapse itself serves as the celebration video.

evercam_reduction_pct.rationale: Replacement role — Evercam's time-lapse footage provides the raw material for a compelling completion video. Some branding and editing may still be needed for high-profile handovers.

assumptions.model_note: This workflow uses alternative cost (videographer hire) rather than internal time saving. Formula: saving = alternative_cost × evercam_reduction_pct × deliverables_per_project.

incidents_per_year.rationale: Perimeter breaches including trespass, attempted theft, vandalism, and unauthorised access. Higher frequency than theft-specific incidents because includes all boundary events.

incidents_prevented_pct.rationale: Replacement role — visible cameras on perimeter serve as primary deterrent. Effectiveness depends on camera coverage and signage. Does not physically prevent access but deters opportunistic breaches.

investigation_time_saved_hours.rationale: Perimeter breach investigations are typically shorter than theft investigations. With footage: identify breach point and timing quickly. Without: walk entire perimeter, check for damage, interview staff.

guard_cost_offset.rationale: Replacement role — cameras can partially replace physical perimeter patrols. Conservative: no guard replacement (cameras supplement only). Base: 4 hours/week of patrol replaced by camera monitoring. Optimistic: one full shift per week eliminated.

assumptions.guard_hourly_rate_note: Use security_guard_hourly_rate from benchmarks if guard_cost_offset > 0.
assumptions.double_counting_note: Overlap with #28 (After-Hours Security) and #29 (Theft Investigation). This workflow covers perimeter-specific monitoring; #28 covers after-hours events; #29 covers theft investigation specifically. Avoid counting the same incident in multiple workflows.

incidents_per_year.rationale: Vehicle/plant incidents on construction sites: collisions, struck-by events, overturn, reversing incidents. HSE data shows plant/vehicle incidents are a leading cause of construction fatalities. On a mid-size site with regular plant activity, 1–4 reportable or near-miss events per year.

investigation_hours_without_evercam.rationale: Vehicle incident investigation without footage: scene examination, operator interview, witness collection, plant inspection, reconstruction. Typically 1.5 days of H&S manager time.

investigation_hours_with_evercam.rationale: With footage: review camera recording of incident, identify sequence, export evidence, write report. Vehicle incidents are particularly well-captured by fixed cameras because they occur in open areas (roads, laydown, crane zones).

investigation_time_saved_pct.rationale: Derived: (12-5)/12 = 58%. Same pattern as #20 but slightly lower because vehicle incidents often require physical plant inspection regardless of footage availability.

claims_defended_pct.rationale: Footage is especially powerful for vehicle incidents — clearly shows who was at fault, whether exclusion zones were breached, whether banksman was present. Strong evidence for insurance and legal defence.

avg_claim_value.note: Vehicle/plant incidents tend to be more severe (and more expensive) than average construction injuries. Consider applying a severity multiplier of 1.5–2x.

workflow_assumptions.workflow_name: Safety Training & Lessons Learned Using Site Footage

training_sessions_per_year.rationale: Safety toolbox talks and lessons-learned sessions that benefit from real site footage. Monthly is typical; weekly on larger or higher-risk sites.

manual_hours_per_session_without_evercam.rationale: Without site footage: H&S manager must create training materials from scratch — sourcing generic stock photos/videos, staging re-enactments, or relying on text-based descriptions of incidents. ~3 hours preparation per session.

manual_hours_per_session_with_evercam.rationale: With Evercam: pull actual site footage of the incident or near-miss, annotate, present directly. Real footage is more impactful than generic materials. ~1 hour preparation.

assumptions.indirect_value_note: The indirect value of better training materials (using real incidents rather than generic content) is significant but not quantified in this model. Real footage creates more impactful training, potentially reducing future incident rates.

disputes_per_year.rationale: Concrete pour disputes: timing (was the pour on schedule?), quality (was curing time adequate?), defects (was the process followed?). On a project with regular concrete works, 1–4 disputed pours per year requiring evidence review.

avg_dispute_value.rationale: Concrete disputes can be very expensive — remedial work for a failed pour ranges from minor patching (£5K) to demolish-and-repour (£50K+). The wide range reflects variation in pour size and structural importance.

disputes_resolved_by_footage_pct.rationale: Supporting role — time-stamped footage proves when pours started/finished, weather conditions during curing, and whether correct processes were followed. Does not capture all quality factors (mix design, testing), but provides strong evidence on process compliance.

disputes_per_year.rationale: Defect disputes with subcontractors are frequent on most projects. Scales with subcontractor count. On a project with 20+ subcontractors, multiple defect disputes per month during active phases.

avg_dispute_value.rationale: Per-defect dispute value: cost of remediation + investigation time + potential back-charge dispute. Varies widely from minor finish defects to major structural issues.

disputes_resolved_by_footage_pct.rationale: Supporting role — footage shows work in progress, making it possible to identify when defects were introduced and by which trade. Particularly useful for hidden work (covered up by subsequent trades). 360 captures add interior evidence.

assumptions.double_counting_note: Partial overlap with #33 (attendance verification) and #34 (invoice disputes). This workflow specifically covers quality/defect disputes, not payment or attendance. However, the same subcontractor relationship may generate disputes in multiple categories — ensure the dispute count is not inflated.

overcharges_prevented_per_year.rationale: Plant hire overcharges: equipment on site but not working, equipment removed early but hire period claimed in full, incorrect equipment substituted. On projects with significant plant hire, several overcharge instances per year.

avg_overcharge_value.rationale: Per-instance overcharge: typically a few days of unnecessary plant hire at £200–£1,000/day, or a disputed utilisation claim. Large plant (cranes, piling rigs) overcharges can be significantly higher.

evercam_detection_pct.rationale: Supporting role — cameras can verify whether plant is on site and whether it is being actively used. Gate Report with ANPR tracks when plant arrives and leaves. Fixed cameras show utilisation patterns. Does not capture off-camera areas or detailed operating hours.

workflow_assumptions.workflow_name: Pay Application / Progress Claim Visual Verification

overcharges_prevented_per_year.rationale: Progress claims that overstate completion. On a project with 20+ subcontractors submitting monthly applications, at least a few per year will claim more than actual progress. QS typically catches most, but footage adds verification.

avg_overcharge_value.rationale: Per-instance overpayment prevented: typically 5–15% of a monthly application value for the relevant subcontractor. On a £100K monthly application, a 10% overstatement is £10K.

evercam_detection_pct.rationale: Supporting role — visual progress verification supplements QS physical site walks. Cameras and 360 captures provide timestamped evidence of actual progress. Particularly useful for disputed areas where QS assessment differs from subcontractor claim. Not all progress is visually verifiable from camera positions.

assumptions.additional_value_note: Beyond preventing overpayment, visual verification speeds the certification process — QS can pre-assess progress remotely before the formal site walk.

workflow_assumptions.workflow_name: Dispute Resolution — Legal Evidence Retrieval & Formal Claims

formal_disputes_per_project.rationale: Formal disputes (adjudication, arbitration, litigation) per project. Not all projects have formal disputes, but when they occur, they are expensive. Industry data: 30–40% of UK construction projects involve some form of formal dispute.

avg_formal_dispute_cost.rationale: Cost of formal dispute resolution: legal fees + expert fees + management time + potential adverse outcome. KCL adjudication data: mean referred sum £291K, typical referral cost £4,500. But total dispute cost including legal team, expert witnesses, and management distraction is much higher.

disputes_avoided_or_reduced_by_footage_p.rationale: Supporting role — visual evidence can resolve disputes before they escalate to formal proceedings, or strengthen position in adjudication/litigation. Footage is admissible evidence and can be decisive. Conservative because many disputes are about contract interpretation, not facts on the ground.

assumptions.double_counting_note: Careful overlap with #33 (attendance), #34 (invoice), #41 (variation). This workflow covers disputes that have escalated to formal proceedings. The earlier workflows cover pre-escalation resolution. Model should include only the incremental value of formal dispute support, not re-count the prevention value already captured in other workflows.

overcharges_prevented_per_year.rationale: Earthworks and stockpile quantity disputes: volume of material moved, fill placed, or stockpile quantities. Mainly relevant to civil/infrastructure projects with significant earthworks.

avg_overcharge_value.rationale: Per-instance: difference between claimed and actual volumes × unit rate. Earthworks rates of £5–£20/m3 mean a 500m3 discrepancy is £2.5K–£10K.

evercam_detection_pct.rationale: Supporting role — drone-based aerial surveys provide volume calculations that can be compared against contractor claims. Fixed cameras provide time-stamped evidence of material movement. Does not replace formal survey but provides supplementary evidence and more frequent measurement points.

assumptions.sector_applicability_note: Primarily applicable to civil engineering, infrastructure, and large-scale earthworks projects. Limited value on building-only projects.

workflow_assumptions.workflow_name: Dig Permit & Underground Utility Clearance Documentation

disputes_per_year.rationale: Utility strike or dig permit disputes are occasional but consequential. Not all projects involve significant excavation. When they occur, proving that proper clearance procedures were followed is critical for liability defence.

avg_dispute_value.rationale: Utility strike costs: repair + third-party claims + delay + potential regulatory fine. A gas main strike can cost £20K–£100K+. Water main: £5K–£50K. The wide range reflects variation in utility type and damage severity.

disputes_resolved_by_footage_pct.rationale: Supporting role — footage provides evidence of dig permit procedures being followed, location of excavation, and conditions at the time of the strike. Useful for liability defence but does not prevent the strike itself. 360 captures of trench conditions add value.

assumptions.frequency_note: Occasional occurrence — not every project has utility strike risks. Model should apply this workflow only when the project profile indicates excavation work.

rework_rate_pct.note: Uses conservative/base/optimistic from the benchmark data. MEP rework rates tend to be at the higher end of the range due to system complexity.

early_detection_pct.rationale: Percentage of MEP commissioning rework detectable through 360 captures and camera footage. Lower than BIM comparison (#51) because commissioning issues are often functional rather than visual. However, 360 captures can identify installation defects, missing components, and deviations from design before systems are energised.

evercam_contribution_pct.rationale: Supporting role — Evercam provides visual verification but does not replace functional testing. Contribution is lower than #51 (BIM comparison) because commissioning relies heavily on performance data, not just visual inspection.

assumptions.phase_note: This workflow is active during the MEP installation and commissioning phases — typically the final 30–40% of the project timeline.
assumptions.sector_applicability_note: Most relevant to projects with significant MEP scope — commercial, healthcare, data centres, industrial.

event_probability_per_year.rationale: Serious crane/lift incident probability per site per year. HSE data: ~4,000 crane operations per fatal/major injury. On a typical site with a tower crane operating for 12 months, the probability of a serious incident is approximately 2%. This is conservative — many sites operate without incident for years.

event_cost.rationale: Total cost of a serious crane incident: investigation + regulatory fine + legal costs + project delay + potential compensation claim + equipment damage. HSE prosecutions for crane incidents regularly result in £100K–£500K fines alone. Total cost including delay and claims can exceed £1M for fatalities.

probability_reduction_pct.rationale: Evercam provides real-time exclusion zone monitoring, enabling supervisors to identify unsafe conditions before they cause incidents. Conservative because cameras supplement but do not replace physical safety measures. The primary value is in catching near-misses that would otherwise escalate.

cost_mitigation_pct.rationale: If an incident occurs, footage significantly reduces investigation cost, supports regulatory defence, and can demonstrate that safety protocols were in place. Reduces the total incident cost by providing clear evidence rather than relying on witness accounts.

workflow_assumptions.workflow_name: Fire Investigation & Hot Work Safety Monitoring

event_probability_per_year.rationale: Probability of a significant fire event on a construction site per year. Construction sites are high fire risk due to hot work, temporary electrical, flammable materials. UK Fire Statistics: ~2,000 construction fires per year across ~300,000 active sites. ~0.7% site-level annual rate, but not all are significant. 3% for fires requiring formal investigation.

event_cost.rationale: Cost of a significant construction fire: damage repair + project delay + regulatory investigation + potential prosecution + insurance excess + temporary works. Grenfell-scale events are excluded (those are catastrophic, not typical). A typical significant fire: £50K–£500K total impact.

probability_reduction_pct.rationale: Cameras can monitor hot work areas and detect early signs of fire (smoke, flame). Real-time monitoring enables faster response. However, cameras do not prevent ignition — they enable earlier detection and faster intervention. Value is primarily in reducing the severity of fires that do start.

cost_mitigation_pct.rationale: If a fire occurs, footage identifies the cause and origin (critical for insurance claims and prosecution defence), proves whether hot work permits were being followed, and demonstrates the fire response timeline. Strong evidence value for insurance recovery and regulatory defence.

event_probability_per_year.rationale: Probability of a serious incident in a restricted/high-risk zone per year. Restricted zones exist because they are inherently dangerous — excavations, live services, confined spaces, demolition areas. 3% accounts for unauthorised entry leading to a serious incident.

event_cost.rationale: Cost of a serious incident in a restricted zone: injury/fatality costs + regulatory prosecution + project shutdown + legal liability. HSE takes a particularly strict view of failures to control access to restricted areas.

probability_reduction_pct.rationale: Replacement role — Evercam provides continuous monitoring of restricted zones, replacing or supplementing physical barriers and periodic checks. Camera monitoring with alerts can detect unauthorised entry in real-time. Higher reduction than supporting-role workflows because this is a primary monitoring function.

cost_mitigation_pct.rationale: If an incident occurs in a restricted zone, footage proves whether access controls were in place and whether the injured party was authorised. Strong evidence for regulatory defence and liability limitation.

event_probability_per_year.rationale: Probability of a compliance event (stop-work order, formal complaint requiring investigation, environmental notice) on an urban construction site per year. Higher probability than safety events because community complaints are common on urban sites. 10% reflects sites with sensitive neighbours.

event_cost.rationale: Cost of a compliance event: stop-work delay (£5K–£20K/day × 1–5 days) + investigation/remediation + community liaison + potential planning condition breach fine. A 3-day stop-work order on a £20M project costs ~£30K in delay alone.

probability_reduction_pct.rationale: Replacement role — cameras provide evidence of operating hours compliance, dust/noise mitigation measures in place, and site activity patterns. Proactive monitoring can identify compliance risks before they trigger complaints. Does not prevent all community issues but demonstrates good faith and due diligence.

cost_mitigation_pct.rationale: If a complaint or enforcement action occurs, timestamped footage proves compliance (or identifies the specific breach). Can turn a stop-work order into a warning, or demonstrate that the complaint was unfounded. Strong evidence for planning authority and environmental regulator engagement.

assumptions.sector_applicability_note: Most relevant to urban sites, sites near residential areas, and projects with strict planning conditions. Limited value on remote/rural sites.

event_probability_per_year.rationale: Probability of a formal regulatory investigation (HSE visit resulting in enforcement action, OSHA citation, or formal prosecution) per site per year. HSE conducts ~5,000 construction inspections per year across ~300,000 sites, but not all result in enforcement. 5% accounts for sites that receive formal enforcement action.

event_cost.rationale: Cost of formal regulatory enforcement: fine (HSE average construction fine: £50K–£150K post-sentencing guidelines) + legal fees (£20K–£50K) + management time (£10K–£30K) + reputational damage (unquantified). Total £80K–£230K for a typical prosecution. Conservative estimate of £100K.

probability_reduction_pct.rationale: Cameras do not prevent regulatory investigations, but proactive monitoring can identify non-compliance before an inspector arrives. The probability reduction represents issues caught and corrected before they become enforcement triggers.

cost_mitigation_pct.rationale: If a prosecution occurs, footage is powerful evidence: demonstrates safety management systems were in place, shows compliance history, supports due diligence defence. Sentencing guidelines consider the organisation's safety culture — footage demonstrating active monitoring is strong mitigation. Can reduce fine levels significantly.

event_probability_per_year.rationale: Probability of a formal operating hours breach event on a constrained urban site per year. Higher than general compliance (#45) because this is specifically focused on sites with strict operating hour restrictions. On constrained sites (hospital adjacency, residential, city centre), breaches are common and complaints frequent.

event_cost.rationale: Cost of an operating hours breach: formal warning then breach of planning condition then potential injunction. Typical cost: council investigation + legal response + potential fine + delay while remediation plan is agreed. Lower than general environmental compliance because the consequence is typically a warning/fine rather than a full stop-work order.

probability_reduction_pct.rationale: Replacement role — cameras with timestamps provide definitive proof of operating hours compliance. Real-time monitoring can alert site managers when work continues past permitted hours. Higher reduction than #45 because operating hours are binary (working/not working) and easily verified by camera footage.

cost_mitigation_pct.rationale: If a complaint is made, timestamped footage can definitively prove that work stopped at the permitted time, or identify the specific breach (which subcontractor, what activity). This can turn a formal enforcement action into a documented one-off with a clear corrective action. Strong evidence for planning authority engagement.

assumptions.double_counting_note: Overlap with #45 (Noise, Community & Environmental Compliance). This workflow is specifically about operating hours on constrained sites; #45 covers broader environmental/community compliance. When both are applicable, the model should use the higher probability/cost from the two, not sum them.
